jobs.title: Land Survey Technician
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Survey Instrument Operator / Land Survey Technician
to support a variety of land surveying projects. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working outdoors, is comfortable with technology and mathematics, and takes pride in accurate, precise fieldwork.

Prior surveying experience is preferred but not required. Training will be provided to the right candidate.

What You'll Be Doing

Working alongside a Survey Crew Chief and, at times, independently, you will support a variety of surveying projects, including:

Monument reconnaissance
Boundary surveys
ALTA/NSPS Land Title Surveys
Topographic surveys
Aerial photo control
Construction stakeout
Survey research

You Will

Perform essential field tasks supporting daily survey crew operations
Collect accurate, high-quality field data
Prepare clear field notes and sketches
Operate and maintain survey equipment and vehicles
Follow field safety procedures and maintain professional standards
Collaborate with office staff to support efficient project completion

Equipment & Technical Experience

Aptitude and willingness to learn surveying techniques and technology
Previous experience operating survey equipment is a strong plus
Ability to learn and properly use field surveying instruments and related technology

Qualifications

Valid driver's license
Ability to work independently as well as part of a team
Comfortable working outdoors in varying weather conditions
Strong attention to detail and accuracy
Safety-conscious approach to fieldwork
Willingness to travel overnight occasionally is a plus
Strong work ethic and dependable attendance

Compensation & Benefits

401(k) with profit-sharing and bonus opportunities
Health, dental, and vision insurance
Long- and short-term disability insurance
Life insurance
Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
Health Reimbursement Arrangement (HRA)
Paid time off
Professional development assistance
Tuition reimbursement

jobs.title: Data Analyst, New Grad
jobs.description:
Jobright is your personal AI job search agent that transforms the way you do job search from solo, time-consuming efforts to a fast, expert-guided journey, simplifying every job search step and accelerating your route to the best job outcomes. As a Data Analyst, New Grad, you will work onsite with product, engineering, and AI teams to turn product, job market, and user data into insights that directly influence product development.

Why Join Us

• Build real, production AI agents used by real users
• High ownership and impact
• Work at the intersection of AI, agents, and product
• Shape how people experience AI-driven job search

Responsibilities

• Analyze product, user, and job market data to identify trends and opportunities
• Write SQL queries and build reports, dashboards, and analytical tools
• Define and monitor key product and business metrics
• Support A/B tests and evaluate new product features
• Investigate data quality issues and improve reporting accuracy
• Present findings to product, engineering, and business stakeholders
• Collaborate closely with the team in an onsite environment
Qualification

Required

• Recent graduate or graduating soon in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics, or a related field
• Strong SQL skills and familiarity with spreadsheets or Python
• Understanding of basic statistics, data analysis, and experimentation
• Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
• Ability to work onsite in the SF Bay Area

Preferred

• Experience with pandas, scikit-learn, Tableau, Looker, or similar tools
• Familiarity with product analytics, recommendation systems, or search
• Experience working with large or messy datasets
• Previous internship, research, or analytics project experience

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Job Title: Construction Project Coordinator

Employment Type: Full-Time

Location: The Hamptons, NY

Work Arrangement: Office and field-based

Reports To: Construction Project Coordinator

The Opportunity

You will be the central point of communication between project managers, field teams, vendors, and clients, providing day-to-day administrative support for our operations.

This role requires exceptional organizational skills, multitasking, detailed record-keeping, deep technical knowledge, and the ability to adapt quickly to new software and systems. This is an in-person position and cannot be done remotely.

Primary Responsibilities

Coordinate project schedules, resources, and communications to ensure timely project completion.
Maintain and organize project documentation, contracts, permits, and reports.
Use Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, etc.) to track, share, and present project information.
Learn and implement new project management and construction-related software as needed.
Serve as a liaison between field teams, management, and clients to provide updates and resolve issues.
Monitor project timelines, budgets, and deliverables; alert stakeholders to potential risks or delays.
Support procurement by tracking orders, deliveries, and vendor communications.

Qualifications/Experience

Proven experience in construction coordination, project management, or a related role.
Deep knowledge of technology and ability to quickly learn new programs.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Familiarity with construction terminology, documentation, and workflows.

Technology Skills

Preferred experience with:

JobTread (preferred) or similar.
AutoCAD (review level).
Microsoft Excel (advanced).
Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, etc.).
Adobe Acrobat.
ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity (and similar).

Compensation & Benefits

salary

Professional development opportunities
Collaborative, creative work environment

jobs.title: Architectural Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
Ready to take ownership of real projects and grow your architecture career with a team that's got your back? Let's talk.

Interplan has spent 50+ years designing restaurant and retail spaces for major national brands and has offices in Orlando and Chicago. Our Orlando team is growing, and we're looking for an Architectural Project Coordinator who's ready to run projects with autonomy while learning from experienced architects and managers along the way.
What you'll be doing:

Producing construction documents that bring designs to life
Running a small project or series of small projects with minimal oversight
Solving design challenges and keeping work on budget and on time
Delegating and reviewing CAD Technicians' work
Researching and applying codes, with some direct agency interaction
Leading kick-off meetings and coordinating with engineering teams
Partnering with the Project Architect/Manager to deliver great client service

What we're looking for:

3+ years of commercial architecture experience
Bachelor's degree in architecture or equivalent drafting/design experience
Proficiency in AutoCAD, Photoshop, and SketchUp (Revit a plus)
Solid understanding of zoning, building codes, and MEP systems
Strong communication skills and comfort working independently or on a team
Licensure or working toward it is a plus

Why our team loves working here:

A genuinely collaborative culture where senior architects mentor and invest in your growth
An active, employee-led Activities Committee that keeps things fun outside of deadlines
Real opportunities for continuing education and career advancement
A team that celebrates wins together and shows up for each other

This is a full-time, in-office role based in Orlando, with medical/dental/vision coverage, a 401(k) match, paid holidays + PTO, and performance bonuses that align with the culture.

Apply now and help us design spaces people love.

jobs.title: Community Research Liaison, Sr / Pathways Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Function/Duties of Position

The Community Research Liaison, Sr./ Pathways Program Coordinator is a key member of the University Center for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities (UCEDD), which advances the health, inclusion, and quality of life of Oregonians with disabilities and their families through education, research, community engagement, and workforce development.

The Pathways for Rural Oregon Students to Healthcare and Disability Careers (Pathways) program is an internship and mentorship initiative that helps strengthen Oregon’s rural healthcare workforce and improve services for people with developmental disabilities. Pathways prepare rural students for healthcare and disability-related careers through mentorship, internships, and career development opportunities. This is a grant funded project that is funded through September 30, 2027.

This position supports program planning, implementation, and evaluation; develops and delivers curriculum and training; coordinates internships and mentorships; cultivates community and healthcare partnerships; and leads outreach, recruitment, and participant engagement efforts. Additional responsibilities include event and logistic coordination, data collection, grant reporting, and supporting program operations across multiple stakeholders. The position requires sone travel throughout Oregon and occasional in-state and out-of-state travel for conferences, training sessions, meetings, presentations, and student-focused events.

The ideal candidate is an organized, collaborative professional with strong communication skills, experience managing educational or workforce development programs, proficiency with digital tools and learning platforms, and a commitment to expanding opportunities for rural students.

Required Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor's degree in Education, Public Health, Public Administration, Social Work, Rehabilitation Counseling, Healthcare Administration, Disability Studies, Business Administration, Management, or a related field; AND
two years of relevant experience OR
equivalent combination of education and experience may be substituted.

Experience

The two years of revlevant experience needs to include: coordinating internships, mentorship, workforce development, or educational programs involving students, trainees, or community participants in healthcare, disability, public health, or community-based settings. Relevant experience may also include working with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD), people with disabilities, and their families.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Advanced Microsoft Excel and Word skills
Advanced database management skills
Web based course design and implementation
Strong attention to detail
Excellent organizational skills
Excellent problem-solving skills
Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills
Able to function independently and as part of a team
Ability to work in an interruptive office environment
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Ability to take initiative

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Education, Business Administration, Management, Public Administration, or a field related to the position.
Knowledge of rural communities and Oregon healthcare workforce needs.
Strong facilitation, presentation, and communication skills.
Lived, family, or professional experience related to disability.
Experience with grant-funded programs and reporting.
Experience recruiting, mentoring, or supporting students.
Experience coordinating internship, mentorship, or workforce development programs.
Experience in the field of developmental disabilities.
Personal or professional experience in rural communities.
Experience partnering with individuals with I/DD, families, and community organizations.
Proficiency with Microsoft Teams.

Additional Details

Apply here online:

Upload cover letter and resume. Please be sure to include months and years (MM/YYYY format) to the resume for jobs/work experience.

*OHSU Employees be sure to apply using your OHSU email.*

Why apply to OHSU?

We are Oregon's only public academic health center.

In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington.

All are welcome.

OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply.

To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu
